title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: guess: equiatomic elemental powders of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti mixed in a high-energy ball mill
recollection.intervention: guess: mechanical alloying for extended durations (e.g., 30–60 h) followed by spark plasma sintering at ~950 °C under a pressure of ~50 MPa
recollection.structure: guess: a predominantly single-phase FCC high-entropy solid solution with dispersed nanoscale B2 or Laves-type precipitates after sintering
recollection.mechanism: guess: severe plastic deformation during milling yields ultrafine grains and supersaturation, while rapid SPS heating suppresses grain growth and induces intermetallic nanoprecipitation, leading to hardening via grain-boundary strengthening and precipitation hardening
recollection.results: guess: average microhardness around 850–950 HV (with peak local values exceeding 1000 HV), relative density >99.5%, and grain sizes refined to below 200 nm

score.note: Correctly identifies mechanical alloying followed by SPS and gives a plausible SPS temperature, but the proposed 30–60 h milling duration is far from the actual 1–6 h. The predicted single-phase FCC matrix with B2/Laves precipitates conflicts with the measured 83% FCC/17% BCC structure. Grain-boundary strengthening and milling-induced deformation are relevant, but precipitation hardening is not the reported mechanism; dislocation and solid-solution strengthening are omitted. The hardness estimate (850–950 HV) is substantially above 675 HV, the grain-size estimate is not close to <48 nm, and the reported strength values are absent.
